scope: Scoped pass after the move to GCSE Biology: exam-structure claims, required-practical numbers, tier wrappers, 'not on your course' wording, board naming. Facts were checked separately today.

findings.claim: Reaction time "is Required Practical 6 in the specification", and the collapsible is titled "Required Practical 6: Measuring Reaction Time".
findings.truth: In the GCSE Biology list the reaction-time investigation is required practical 7. Practical 6 is the effect of light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis. 6 was the Combined Science number.
findings.evidence: spec 8.2.7 and 4.5.2.1: "Required practical activity 7: plan and carry out an investigation into the effect of a factor on human reaction time"; 8.2.6 is photosynthesis.

findings.claim: The n4 key fact teaches brain mapping (damage studies, electrical stimulation, MRI) as core content, with no tier wrapper.
findings.truth: Mapping brain regions to functions by those three methods is marked (HT only) in the biology spec. The regions themselves (cerebral cortex, cerebellum, medulla) stay core.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.2.2 The brain (biology only): "(HT only) Neuroscientists have been able to map the regions of the brain to particular functions by studying patients with brain damage, electrically stimulating different parts of the brain and using MRI scanning techniques."

findings.claim: The n10 paragraph (MRI scanning) and the n11 key fact (why brain disorders are hard to treat and investigate) are taught as core content.
findings.truth: Explaining the difficulties of investigating brain function and treating brain damage and disease is marked (HT only).
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.2.2: "(HT only) Students should be able to explain some of the difficulties of investigating brain function and treating brain damage and disease."

findings.claim: A single higher-only wrapper covers the whole kidney block: excretion, the nephron, ultrafiltration, selective reabsorption, water balance and ADH. The wrapper was used to mean "separate science only", and .higher-only is hidden outright for Foundation students.
findings.truth: In the biology spec the kidney's role in water balance, urine production by filtration and selective reabsorption of glucose, some ions and water is core for both tiers. Only the ADH content is (HT only). The wrapper now opens at the Water Balance and ADH heading and closes at its existing tag after the n13 key fact.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.3.3 Maintaining water and nitrogen balance in the body (biology only): the filtration and selective reabsorption statements carry no tier marker; "(HT only) Students should be able to describe the effect of ADH on the permeability of the kidney tubules" and "(HT only) The water level in the body is controlled by the hormone ADH...".

findings.claim: A single higher-only wrapper covers the whole DNA block: DNA as a polymer of nucleotides, the four bases, the double helix, complementary base pairing, protein synthesis, mutations and the lesson diagram.
findings.truth: DNA as a polymer of two strands in a double helix, the gene definition, the nucleotide make-up, the four bases and the triplet code are core in the biology spec. Complementary base pairing (C-G, T-A), protein synthesis and mutations are (HT only). The wrapper now opens at the n4 key fact and closes before the diagram.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.1.4 DNA and the genome (core, both tiers) and 4.6.1.5 DNA structure (biology only) - the polymer, nucleotide and triplet statements carry no tier marker, while "(HT only) In the complementary strands a C is always linked to a G...", "(HT only) Proteins are synthesised on ribosomes..." and the mutation statements do.

findings.claim: Eight cards are prefixed "(Higher)". Four of them are core content: the polymer/nucleotide card, the double-helix card, the gene card and the triplet-code card.
findings.truth: Those four are core in the biology spec, so the label wrongly tells a Foundation student the card is not theirs. The base-pairing, mRNA, ribosome and mutation cards keep the label.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.1.4 and the non-HT statements of 4.6.1.5.

findings.claim: The n2 paragraph teaches deamination of excess amino acids in the liver, now inside core content.
findings.truth: Deamination is (HT only) in the biology spec. It sits in the middle of a core narration block, so wrapping it would split a data-narration-id span. Foundation students seeing extra content is a small cost; the block cannot be wrapped surgically.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.3.3: "(HT only) The digestion of proteins from the diet results in excess amino acids...deaminated to form ammonia...converted to urea".

findings.claim: The "How the Nephron Works" section teaches the glomerulus, Bowman's capsule and the afferent/efferent arterioles.
findings.truth: The biology spec states that the structure of the kidney and of a nephron is not required. The content is correct but beyond the spec, and it is now core rather than hidden. Worth a trim on a content pass, not a tier fix.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.3.3: "Knowledge of other parts of the urinary system, the structure of the kidney and the structure of a nephron is not required."

findings.claim: The n17 paragraph teaches complementary base pairing (A-T, C-G) as core, with no tier wrapper.
findings.truth: Complementary base pairing is (HT only) in the biology spec. Lesson 11 now carries the same content correctly wrapped, so lesson 4 over-teaches rather than under-teaches. Left alone to avoid touching a copied lesson beyond the brief.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.1.5: "(HT only) In the complementary strands a C is always linked to a G on the opposite strand and a T to an A."

findings.claim: The n33 paragraph gives the restriction-enzyme and plasmid-vector steps of genetic engineering as core.
findings.truth: The steps of genetic engineering are (HT only). Lesson 7 wraps the same content correctly. This is over-teaching, not lost entitlement, so no edit.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.2.4: "(HT only) Students should be able to describe the main steps in the process of genetic engineering."

verified_correct: No exam-structure claim anywhere in the unit mentions six papers, 1h15, 70 marks, Combined Science or Trilogy. Lesson 4 already says "Biology Paper 2", which is right for two papers of 1h45 and 100 marks each.
No sentence says a topic is 'not on your course', 'separate science only' or 'beyond the combined course'.
No exam board is named in any student-facing field.

Higher-only wrappers checked and left in place: lesson 2 (glucagon, negative feedback, thyroxine, adrenaline - spec 4.5.2.2 HT and 4.5.3.7 HT only); lesson 3 (FSH/LH/oestrogen/progesterone interactions - spec 4.5.3.4 HT; infertility treatment - spec 4.5.3.6 HT only); lesson 7 (steps of genetic engineering - spec 4.6.2.4 HT only); lesson 10 second wrapper (gibberellins and ethene - spec 4.5.4.1 HT only, and plant hormone uses - spec 4.5.4.2 HT only); the '(Higher)' flashcards in lessons 2 and 3.
The phototropism practical in lesson 10 and the milk decay practical in lesson 13 carry no practical number, so nothing to renumber; both methods match biology practicals 8 and 10.
summary: Six FIX findings across four lessons, all tier or numbering. Two higher-only wrappers had been used to mean 'separate science only' and hid core kidney and DNA content from Foundation students; both are now split at the real HT boundary. Lesson 1 carried the Combined Science practical number for reaction time. Lesson 9 needed brain mapping wrapping as HT only. No combined-science exam-structure claim survives in this unit.
